newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply up on deregulation steps.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply up on deregulation steps.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply higher on Tuesday, boosted by the finance ministry's plans to further ease controls on the local securities industry, brokers said.
They said investor sentiment improved in views that the collapse of two steelmakers were unlikely to cause a chain reaction of corporate failures.
The composite index added 3.51 percent, or 21.64 points, to close at 638.90.
"Investors regained confidence after the recent week-long falls. The plan to ease rules on stock trading helped improve sentiment," said Lee Kye-joon of Daishin Securities.
Trading was active, with 42.95 million shares changing hands, compared with 36.2 million on Monday.
Advancers outpaced losers by 733 to 131, with 221 shares rising to their daily upper limits.
But some brokers called for caution, saying much of Tuesday's rise stemmed from a technical rebound following the past six straight days of declines.
"The market is still vulnerable to non-economic factors like the reopened probe into the Hanbo scandal," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
Prosecutors reopened last week a loans-for-kickbacks scandal surrounding failed Hanbo Steel Co.

On Tuesday, finance ministry officials said the ministry plans to allow local brokerages to issue corporate bonds and hold up to 15 percent of a listed company's shares issued, up from the current five percent.
Analysts say these steps would help boost earnings of brokerages and give a freer hand to brokerages in fund management.
